Antigravity pump lifts water upwards with no power source

I think, rather than "how tall can the water column be?", the most relevant questions are "how wide can it be?" and "how pure does it need to be?"; if the answers are "very" and "potable", I forsee potential applications in this technique's future.

Have you ever wondered how trees that are hundreds of feet tall get water to their tops? This is exactly that mechanism, albeit with a few tweaks. The molecular structure of water creates ends with a slightly negative charge on one side and a slightly positive charge on the other. This means that all water molecules have a weak electrical attraction to each other and the phenomenon is called cohesion. That's why this pump starts working when water falls out the other side of the pipe. The falling water is literally pulling all the water behind it. Hope that makes sense.
